purpose: Demonstrate, reproducibly and on shipped code, that a well-formed negative control can be correctly rejected and still fail to exercise the state it was written to test.
principle: Each case names the decision state the mutation was WRITTEN to test. The prediction below was recorded before the run. A case is 'shadowed' when both implementations reject it, as intended, but at an earlier state than the one it targets — which a boolean pass/fail suite reports as a success.
note: The naive and refined operators differ only in whether the receipt's witness reference to the mutated entry is cleared, and the receipt re-signed, before the entry is altered.

cases.rationale: The receipt still names overt_receipt.sig in witness.signature_refs, so the witness-reference check rejects the package before the signed-receipt gate is reached.
Clearing the witness reference and re-signing the receipt first removes the earlier guard, so the intended state decides.
The receipt still names timestamp.tsr in witness.timestamp_refs, so the witness-reference check rejects the package before the RFC 3161 state is reached.
Clearing the timestamp witness reference and re-signing first removes the earlier guard.
